title: Creation: God and man in covenant
text: God makes the world good and man in his image, to know and serve him. The Reformed confessions describe a covenant of works with Adam, with life promised for obedience [WCF VII.2]. Hosea 6:7 is read in more than one way. [INTRA-REFORMED DEBATE]

title: The fall, and the first promise
text: Adam breaks the covenant, and sin and death enter the world. God at once promises a seed who will crush the serpent (3:15). This is the beginning of the covenant of grace [WCF VII.3]. The gospel was “first revealed in paradise” [HC Q&A 19].

title: Noah: God preserves the world
text: The flood judges the world, and God makes a covenant with Noah and all creatures never to destroy the earth by flood. The rainbow is its sign. It keeps the world in order until the promise is fulfilled.

title: Abraham: the promise of a people and a blessing
text: God calls Abraham and promises a land, a people and blessing for all nations. Circumcision is the sign. Paul teaches that the promise is received by faith, and that Christ is the true seed.

title: Moses: redemption and the law
text: God redeems Israel from Egypt and gives the law, the tabernacle and the sacrifices at Sinai, with the land to follow. The law shows God’s holiness and sin’s guilt, and the sacrifices point forward to Christ. The Westminster Confession calls this the one covenant of grace under the law [WCF VII.5].

title: David: the king and the kingdom
text: God promises David a son whose throne will last for ever (2 Sam 7). The temple is built under Solomon. The Psalms and wisdom books come from this time. The king is the anointed one, “messiah,” who points to the Son of David.

title: Exile, return and the prophets
text: The kingdom divides and falls. Israel goes to Assyria and Judah to Babylon, as the covenant curses had warned. The prophets accuse Israel and promise a new covenant, a new heart and a coming king. A remnant returns and builds the temple, and the Old Testament ends with the promise of a messenger. After about 400 years comes Christ.

title: Christ: the promises fulfilled
text: The Son becomes man, lives under the law, dies as the sacrifice for sin and rises. In him all the promises are “Yes” (2 Cor 1:20), and the whole Old Testament speaks of him (Lk 24:27, 44). The new covenant is sealed in his blood.

title: The church: the covenant to all nations
text: The Spirit is poured out, and the gospel goes to Jew and Gentile alike. The same covenant of grace is now administered through the Word and the two sacraments, baptism and the Lord’s Supper, no longer by the old ceremonies [WCF VII.6]. Christians differ on baptism and on how Israel and the church relate. [INTRA-REFORMED DEBATE] Dispensational and Lutheran readings differ again. [EXTRA-CONFESSIONAL]

title: Consummation: the new creation
text: Christ returns, raises the dead, judges, and makes all things new. God dwells with his people for ever. The timing and order are debated. [INTRA-REFORMED DEBATE]
